review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read the definitions of hardSphereFreeIndex, hardSphereFreeParticleIndex and hardSpherePosition in HardSphereNBC.lean, and the uses of hardSphereFreeParticleIndex_freeIndex and the ScalarShear lemmas across LeanPool. I did not run Lean, so every claim about simp behaviour is a prediction. The two findings are modest. Both are missing-simp-lemma issues, not loops or competing rules. I found no rewrite cycles or orientation problems in this file's simp interface. The remaining lemmas are existence and measurability facts for which simp attributes would not be appropriate.

findings.problem: This is the canonical round-trip identity between the two index conversions. It has no @[simp] attribute, although its sibling hardSpherePosition_free is simp. Without it, simp cannot cancel `hardSphereFreeParticleIndex (hardSphereFreeIndex v hv)`. Downstream code works around this by hand: HardSphereTreeDifference.lean rewrites with `show hardSphereTreeParent hT i = hardSphereFreeParticleIndex p by symm; exact hardSphereFreeParticleIndex_freeIndex ...`. HardSphereNBC.lean reproves the opposite round trip inside hardSpherePosition_free. The file's own proof of hardSphereTreeParent_index_lt uses an explicit `rw` for the same cancellation. The dual fact `hardSphereFreeParticleIndex i ≠ 0` is also reproved by hand, with a `congrArg Fin.val` plus `simp` block, in hardSphereTree_parent_exists (`hv : v ≠ 0`) and in hardSpherePosition_free (`hne`). It has no reusable lemma.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `hardSphereFreeParticleIndex_freeIndex` with `@[simp]`. Its LHS is a function application with the proof argument `hv`, so it is a well-formed simp lemma. The statement has no side goal beyond `hv`, which appears in the LHS. Also add a small lemma `hardSphereFreeParticleIndex_ne_zero (i : Fin (k - 1)) : hardSphereFreeParticleIndex i ≠ 0` (marked simp), and use it in hardSphereTree_parent_exists and in hardSpherePosition_free. Optionally add a simp lemma `hardSpherePosition r v = r (hardSphereFreeIndex v hv)` for `hv : v ≠ 0`. Together these would let the `hpos` step in hardSphereTreeDifferenceFlatBlock_eq close with plain `simp`.
findings.benefit: Terms of the form free-particle-index of free-index normalise automatically. This removes the manual `show … by symm; exact …` rewrite in HardSphereTreeDifference.lean. It also removes duplicated `Fin.val` arithmetic across files, and makes `simp [hchild]` style proofs about tree parents less brittle.

findings.excerpt: hardSphereScalarShear parent child hpc x child = x child - x parent
findings.problem: hardSphereScalarShear is a def that wraps `Matrix.toLin'` of a transvection matrix. Its only usable evaluation interface is these three lemmas, and none of them is tagged @[simp]. A goal like `hardSphereScalarShear p c h x c` stays opaque to `simp` unless each lemma is passed by hand. The `of_ne` and `parent` lemmas overlap, because the parent case is the same as `q = parent` with `parent ≠ child`. Each of the three proofs repeats the same `change (Matrix.mulVec (Matrix.transvection …) x) _ ; rw [...]` unfolding. The three lemmas are not applied anywhere else in LeanPool, so their intended usage form is unspecified.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `hardSphereScalarShear_apply_child` with `@[simp]`, since its RHS is in the desired normal form `x child - x parent`. Mark `hardSphereScalarShear_apply_of_ne` with `@[simp]` too. Its side condition `q ≠ child` is a simple hypothesis that simp can discharge from `hqc` or from `ne_eq` facts. Derive `hardSphereScalarShear_apply_parent` as a corollary of `_of_ne` with `q := parent` and `hpc`, instead of repeating the matrix unfolding. Alternatively, add a single lemma `hardSphereScalarShear_apply (x) (q) : hardSphereScalarShear parent child hpc x q = if q = child then x child - x parent else x q`. With the three apply lemmas as simp lemmas, `simp` can evaluate the shear by case.
findings.benefit: Users of the shear, for example when it is composed with the tree-difference coordinate maps, can evaluate it by `simp` without unfolding `Matrix.toLin'` or `Matrix.transvection`. It also gives one canonical normal form for a coordinate of the sheared vector, and removes the duplicated proof scripts.
